name: position-buildup
description:
A single trader builds a long position over two market buys at different prices, demonstrating the clearing layer's VWAP-style `avg_entry` computation. Alice first buys 10 contracts at 100 (avg_entry = 100), then buys another 10 at 110 (avg_entry weighted to 105). The maker takes the matching short side at the same VWAP. Useful for asking: how does the engine track entry price across multiple fills? What is the unrealized P&L baseline an account is compared against?

Final mark settles back to 100 via a small mark-book so the scenario doesn't trigger liquidations — this is a `walkthrough`, not stress.
headline: Two market buys, 10@100 then 10@110, leave Alice long 20 contracts at avg_entry 105 — VWAP via the clearing layer.

expected_outcomes.name: two-traders
expected_outcomes.description: Exactly 2 accounts touched by trades (Alice + maker)

expected_outcomes.name: two-fills
expected_outcomes.description: Exactly two fills (the two staged market buys)

expected_outcomes.name: fills-bounded
expected_outcomes.description: No surprise fills beyond the two buys

expected_outcomes.name: no-liquidations
expected_outcomes.description: Alice's collateral covers her position; zero liquidation scan-hits (this is a walkthrough, not stress)

expected_outcomes.name: alice-long-20
expected_outcomes.description: Alice ends with +20 long after both market buys

expected_outcomes.name: alice-avg-entry-105
expected_outcomes.description: Alice's avg_entry is the VWAP of the two fills: (10×100 + 10×110) / 20 = 105

expected_outcomes.name: maker-short-20
expected_outcomes.description: Maker ends with the matching -20 short at the same VWAP

expected_outcomes.name: maker-avg-entry-105
expected_outcomes.description: Maker's avg_entry is symmetrically the same VWAP of 105
